summary: UX browser review of Phase 1 'Council fixes' (storytime_look_20261107) at audited HEAD 2c5b3d73f, which equals role_base_sha; git diff 2c5b3d73f..HEAD over apps/storytime/app, apps/storytime/lib and packages/read-along is empty, so no phase file moved. Verdict: pass, no blocking finding, four nonblocking findings and one note. The phase browser gate ran once in the foreground: exit 0, '=== Total: 13 checks (PASS=13, FAIL=0) ===', and the five rows pass (icon_status=200 with console_errors=0 and failed_requests=0; decodable_sentence="A nest."; pages_measured=12 with gap_max_delta_px=0, next_min_height=48 and page_overflow=0; video_preload=metadata with stage_background=1). My own browser run adds the labeled values: the hit area of the one-letter word 'I' is I_hit_w_px=13.27 and I_hit_h_px=39 on the phone and 13.84 by 42 on the tablet and on the phone landscape, with I_effective_tap_w_px=10 to 11, and the neighbour 'Hello' does not steal its tap; the English 404 page renders one 66 px link whose target is /th/st/2/1 (not /en/st/2/1); the shipped w01 holds no wordClips, so clip_words_on_page=0 and words_with_tabindex=0 in all six rows; the 250 ms lyric lag stays a known limit. Next is the filled 48 px button and the three audio buttons are transparent 48 px buttons with the count '1 / 8' in all six rows, with page_overflow_px=0 and clipped_text_count=0. No phone result is claimed: the run is headless Chrome at emulated viewports.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Major] ux-browser-review: the hit area of the one-letter word 'I' in the reader is under the 44 px floor of Q5. Measured (SYSTEM Chrome, th and en): phone 390x844 I_ink_w_px=5.27, I_hit_w_px=13.27, I_hit_h_px=39, I_effective_tap_w_px=10, I_effective_tap_h_px=40; tablet 768x1024 and phone landscape 844x390 I_hit_w_px=13.84, I_hit_h_px=42, I_effective_tap_w_px=11, I_effective_tap_h_px=42. The word stays reachable (the ink centre of 'I' resolves to 'I' and the contiguous tap run holds 10 to 11 px) and the neighbour 'Hello' does not steal its tap (neighbour_effective_tap_w_px=49 to 55 and no neighbour hit area covers the ink centre of 'I'). Rationale: the plan note of task 1.8 accepts the narrow area because a 44 px layout box caused council finding 18, no numbered acceptance criterion of Phase 1 names a 44 px word hit area, and AC-1.9 covers the gaps only. Owner: Green, for the Phase 2 look pass and the look check of 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18.

F2 [Major] ux-browser-review: the tap affordance of a clip word works for a pointer only. Measured (all six locale and viewport rows): clip_words_on_page=0 and words_with_tabindex=0, because the shipped apps/storytime/content/l2/w01.json holds no wordClips key, so no word is a target today; the code gives a target word cursor-pointer, a hover tint and a focus ring, and none of the three shows on a touch screen before a tap. Rationale: the strategy pins only the DOM rule (Q17) and the live check waits for the clip data of Workbooks, so no acceptance criterion of Phase 1 fails. Owner: Green, for Phase 2, as a marker that stays visible on touch at the look check.

F3 [Minor] ux-browser-review: the song lyric line still lights on the timeupdate event, so a line can show up to about 250 ms late (Q22 residual). Rationale: Q22 accepts the lag and the plan asks for the lead-in offset only. Owner: none in this phase; record the lag in the at-home release evidence if a child notices it.

F4 [Major] ux-browser-review: the English 404 page sends the reader to the Thai week page. Measured: notfound_en_status=404, notfound_en_lang=en, notfound_en_links=1, notfound_en_link_href=/th/st/2/1, notfound_en_link_height_px=66, notfound_en_link_text=เปิดสัปดาห์ 1Open week 1; the target shows the Thai tile labels week_page_th_tile_labels=["อ่านตาม","อ่านคำ","เพลง"] against week_page_en_tile_labels=["Read-along","Read the words","Song"]. The cause: apps/storytime/app/[locale]/not-found.tsx reads the locale with getLocale() and falls back to routing.defaultLocale ("th"), and not-found-view.tsx builds the link from that prop. Rationale: AC-1.1 pins the target for the Thai path only and the phase browser gate row 1 accepts either target, so no acceptance criterion of Phase 1 fails; the defect is real for an English reader. Owner: Green; build the link from the locale that parseStorytimePath already returns. The orchestrator should name it for the deploy gate of the at-home release.

F5 [Nit] ux-browser-review: K5 of the adversarial record stays a note for Phase 2: a mode switch during a word clip leaves the clip element playing, so the clip and the sentence audio overlap. Owner: Green, Phase 2.

Carried item (a): the measured values are in F1. The word 'I' is the second word of page 1 ('Hello, I am Pat.') and of page 4 ('Hello, I am Mia.'); the hit area is the pseudo-element of packages/read-along/components/read-along/read-along-passage.tsx (HIT_AREA_CLASSES: before:inset-x-[-0.25rem] before:inset-y-[-0.5rem]), which adds no layout width, so the gap stays even.

Carried item (b): clip_words_on_page=0 and words_with_tabindex=0 in all six rows, and the shipped apps/storytime/content/l2/w01.json holds no wordClips key, so no word of the shipped week is a clip target.
Carried item (d): the measured values are in F4. The English 404 document carries lang=en, so only the link target falls back to the routing default locale.
Carried item (e): K5 stays a note for Phase 2, as F5.

My run counted console_errors=2 and failed_requests=12 over the whole session; the count matches the two 404 documents and the requests aborted by the fast navigation of the harness, and the harness did not record the URLs. The gate row 2 measured console_errors=0 and failed_requests=0 on the two week pages.
No phone result is claimed. The run is headless SYSTEM Chrome at emulated viewports, so it is not a phone check (P1.3 and the row 5 rule of P1.4).

The review harness runs in one heavy job: it starts a throwaway Postgres, applies the migration twice, seeds an account, starts the storage stand-in, builds the app, starts next start in its own process group with setsid, traps EXIT, INT and TERM, and kills the group. The base URL must be http://localhost:<port>: a sign-in from http://127.0.0.1:<port> answers 403 from assertSameOrigin, which the harness setup measured.
